verdicts.reason: Verified byte-exact against disk. ideation-cx.md §3 holds 25 pair blocks; exactly 11 `- **Synthesis**:` lines are hard-truncated — ten at exactly 817 chars (lines 350, 356, 362, 368, 380, 386, 392, 398, 404, 422) and one at exactly 1313 (line 374) — each ending mid-token or mid-clause: :350 "...routes around embar", :362 "...carries as unatteste", :380 "...Near-col", :398 "...third-party licence verificatio", :404 "...authoritatively lifts embar", :422 "...merge retires an identifier — a live". Control: complete blocks at :410 (660 chars) and :416 (813 chars) end with a full stop, and the only other 817-char lines in the whole tree (e.g. 01-identity-profiles-organizations/01.09-party-identifier-resolution.md:74, 21-promotion-marketing/promotion-marketing-index.md:155) end cleanly at a table cell — so 817 is a truncation boundary here, not a coincidence. The file still declares "**Status**: [DEEP]" (ideation-cx.md:5) and "**Last updated**: 2026-07-29" (:6) with no truncation marker. Recoverability is only partial: the 02-03 tail is answered at 03-community-networking/community-networking-cx.md:372 ("must not become visible before the credit publishes (02.01.05 embargo)") and the 02-12 tail is largely restated at ideation-cx.md:82, but the 02-16 tail has no counterpart anywhere — 16-venues-studios-spaces/venues-studios-spaces-cx.md carries no merge/relocation-vs-live-credit rule, and §2's Detail column (ideation-cx.md:56) points at the source domain's CX file, which for 02 (02-credits-attribution/credits-attribution-cx.md) contains only intra-domain CX-01..CX-18 plus a routed-mechanisms table (:333-347) — no per-pair 02↓05/02↓08/02↓16 synthesis at all. Blocking: the truncated halves are cross-domain state-owner/permission/race constraints, and the implementer must invent the missing second half of several of them.

The premise that the id→mechanism mapping must be reverse-engineered is false, and the claimed conflict does not exist. All 31 CX-M ids in live use are bound to a mechanism NAME inline at the point of use, consistently and without a single conflicting binding — e.g. 13-gear-marketplace/gear-marketplace-cx.md:388-390 ("**CX-M04** Atomic Payment ↔ Rights Transfer", "**CX-M31** Safeguarding & Minor Protection", "**CX-M11** Real-Time Rooms, Presence & Audio Transport") and 20-fanbase-direct-to-fan/20.05-memberships-patronage-campaigns/20.05.02-exclusive-content-vault.md:109 ("Consumes **CX-M12 DAW & Desktop Bridge**"). A tree-wide extraction of `CX-M## <Name>` yields a name for every id CX-M01..CX-M32 that is used (CX-M26 is unused), and every one matches domain-map-proposal.md's row order exactly: CX-M01 Payments (:342), CX-M07 Notifications (:348), CX-M08 Reviews (:349), CX-M12 DAW & Desktop Bridge (:353), CX-M14 Shipping (:355), CX-M19 Audit Log (:360), CX-M21 Accessibility (:362), CX-M25 Promoted Placement (:366), CX-M31 Safeguarding (:372), CX-M32 Offline (:373). The "two candidate tables give conflicting answers" claim fails because the ideation-cx.md §1 table (:15-41) carries no id column at all and therefore asserts no mapping — no reader derives ids by counting its rows when 31/31 ids are spelled out with their names in usage. The evidence is also miscounted: the tree has 983 CX-M references, not 830 (132 files is correct). Every competent implementer converges on the same mapping.

The eight systems are absent from ideation-cx.md §1 as claimed, but they are neither undefined nor unowned-by-omission. ideation-index.md:143-144 designates domain-map-proposal.md as the authority for "cross-cuts", that document is "[RATIFIED ...]" (:440), and it defines all eight with purpose and affected domains: Atomic Payment ↔ Rights Transfer (:345), DAW & Desktop Bridge (:353), Onboarding & Role-Aware Activation (:356), Accessibility (:362), Promoted Placement & Advertising (:366), Referrals, Invites & Affiliates (:367), Follow, Save & Watchlist (:369), Offline & Low-Connectivity Field Resilience (:373). The two lists are not the same inventory and are not presented as such: D-25 (ideation-index.md:211) records the §1 registry as "a **25-mechanism cross-cut registry** consolidated from ~235 raw name-buckets" — a separate Step-6 exercise — while D-16 (:202) records the 32-cross-cut map, and D-27 (:213) records a further 52 emergent mechanisms in meta/cross-cut-emergent-capabilities.md. The registry likewise carries four rows absent from the 32 (Split-Capture Trigger, Verified-Credit-as-Evidence, Object & Evidence Storage, Audio Fingerprinting — ideation-cx.md:17, :18, :22, :33), confirming the lists have different provenance rather than one silently dropping rows from the other. Ownership of unowned cross-cuts is explicitly routed, not missing: ideation-cx.md:13 "every row marked `pure-cross-cut` routes to `/create-prd` for ownership", and :12 "pure architecture concerns route to `/create-prd`".

Quote verified verbatim: domain-map-proposal.md:353 "| DAW & Desktop Bridge | Desktop and DAW-host boundary for capture, asset, and workflow integration. | 02 Credits; 07 Music Projects; 14 Digital Goods; 08 Real-Time Jamming; 15 Gear Registry; 22 Analytics. |", inside a document closing "**Status: [RATIFIED ...]**" (:440) and designated the cross-cut authority by ideation-index.md:143-144. D-70 verified at ideation-index.md:255: "**(a) Surface** — no non-web client is authorised", with a four-item named exit. No marker on the row, and the file's not-product routing table (:379-402) does not contain it, so the routing escape does not apply. This is not merely a stale row — the tree has already diverged on it, which is what makes it real rather than cosmetic: 02-credits-attribution/credits-attribution-cx.md:340 marks the mechanism "**NO v1 CHANNEL (owner decision 2026-07-22, D-70 / DQ-08.2)**"; 05-services-marketplace/05.04-delivery-qc-acceptance/05.04-delivery-qc-acceptance-cx.md:110 calls it "Routed to not-product as a hard constraint by the domain map" (a misattribution — it is in the cross-cutting-systems table, not the not-product table); while 12-release-distribution/12.01-release-builder/12.01.04-audio-artwork-asset-conformance.md:244 designs to it unmarked — "the path the design optimises for: masters land from the DAW and never touch a browser upload" — as does 12.03/12.03.03-rejection-triage-remediation.md:97 and 20-fanbase-direct-to-fan/20.05-memberships-patronage-campaigns/20.05.02-exclusive-content-vault.md:109. Warning, not blocking: D-70 is unambiguous and dated in the key file, so the correct build is determinable; the defect is an unmarked ratified row plus four unmarked consumers.

The quoted lines exist (domain-map-proposal.md:60, :84, :144, :240, :252, :264, :288 all list "band" after "**Personas.**"), but they are per-domain audience descriptions in a recovered map, not a persona registry, and they compete with nothing. The persona authority is meta/personas.md, which states its own scope at :3-5 — "Status: `[DEEP]` — 4 primary personas confirmed by owner 2026-07-16 (D-19)", "Consumed by: every domain index Role Matrix (24), every feature file Role Lens", "Short names for Role Matrix columns: **Musician** · **Producer** · **Operator** · **Fan**" — and settles the Band question outright at :38: "The Band is modelled as an **entity** (domain 01), experienced *through* the Musician". Consistent with ideation-index.md:205 (D-19) and :70. No implementer builds ~40 personas from a recovery document's audience lines when the file that every Role Matrix and Role Lens consumes names four and explicitly reclassifies Band; the same document's lines list "insurer", "door staff", "parent/guardian" and "reported user" (:228, :276, :120, :336), which no reading treats as a persona set. Both statements hold simultaneously because they are about different things.

Quote verified (moscow-ledger.md:4 "> **Owner decision (D-20)**: all 195 Must-haves retained; sequencing deferred to `/plan-phase`."; grep D-31 in that file = 0 hits), but the supersession is loudly and correctly marked in the file that governs it. ideation-index.md:206 strikes the exact half at issue — "~~v1 beachhead sequencing deferred to `/plan-phase`~~ **— the "defer the beachhead" half is AMENDED by D-31**" — and :296 repeats "**✅ Sequencing RESOLVED by D-31 (2026-07-18).**". The ledger line is dated provenance, not a live ruling: its own preceding line (:3) reads "Generated from the `/ideate-discover` breadth pass, 2026-07-16", two days before D-31. The residual divergence is also illusory — ideation-index.md:314 keeps `/plan-phase` in the sequencing role ("it orders **within each release** by dependency"), so "sequencing deferred to /plan-phase" and D-31's release split are both still true at different granularities. ideation-index.md is the pipeline key file every downstream workflow reads first, and it answers the question unambiguously.

The arithmetic is correct but nothing turns on it. Disk confirms 189 `*-index.md` and 189 `*-cx.md` below the root (not 190/190), 734 features, 6 meta, 4 root-level files, 1,122 `.md` total; `.memory/wiki/specs/moscow-ledger.md` does not exist while vision.md and feature-ledger.md do; and ideation-index.md:62 asserts "**1,121**" with "`../moscow-ledger.md` live one level up" under the "All counts read from disk" header at :54. But the location error self-resolves inside the same file: ideation-index.md:265, :321, :324 and :327 all link `./moscow-ledger.md`, which is where the file actually is, so any reader following a link lands correctly and never consults the parenthetical. The remaining defect is a ±1 census drift and one uncounted root file — no product behaviour, contract, boundary or scope decision depends on it, and a downstream coverage step enumerates the directory rather than trusting a prose count. Every reasonable reading converges on the same build; this is documentation hygiene, not ambiguity that forces invention.
